payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Jeanene, Layla, Mona, Pauline

payload.content: Hello team, I am Pauline. I have 8 hours available and my top skill is mobile-development with skill level 0.61. I see some tasks related to mobile-development with low priority and some critical priority tasks related to ui-ux-design which are quite costly for me. I am inclined to pick a mobile-development task due to cost and skill match. I would like to know if anyone is targeting the mobile-development implementation or review tasks, so I can decide accordingly to avoid duplicates.

Hello Pauline, this is Mona. I see your interest in mobile-development tasks. I am currently evaluating the low priority mobile-development tasks but have a better skill match with testing tasks. Are you considering specifically the implementation or review tasks for mobile-development? This would help me avoid conflicts as I might lean towards the testing task for mobile-development if it remains unclaimed.

Hi team, Mona here. I am also considering the critical priority tasks related to ui-ux-design, especially the review and test tasks since they match my testing skills better. I would like to know if anyone else is planning to claim those critical priority ui-ux-design tasks so we can avoid overlaps and maximize our sprint rewards.

Hello Pauline and Mona, this is Jeanene. I have 6 hours available with top skills in testing (0.84) and mobile-development (0.64). I am considering the low priority mobile-development test task (ISSUE-0001::test) since it fits my skills and effort within my availability. Pauline, if you are leaning towards mobile-development implementation or review, I can avoid those to prevent conflicts. Mona, if you prioritize critical ui-ux-design tasks, I won't overlap there. Let's coordinate to maximize task coverage without duplication.
